claims.text: A weighted scoring matrix scores each option on each criterion, multiplies each score by the criterion's weight and adds the results, so options strong in different places are compared on one scale.
At stage-4 Đơn Hàng cannot yet email real customers (Mailpit only catches mail in the lab); the team evaluates Dịch vụ A, Dịch vụ B and running its own mail server before real customers arrive.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/email-service-evaluation.md @ stage-4 lines 3-19; docs/adr/0024-dich-vu-gui-email-ben-ngoai.md @ stage-4 lines 11-24; docs/team/self-run-components.md @ stage-4 lines 24-26

claims.text: Knock-out criteria L1-L3 (SMTP with TLS and login; a test environment; export of bounced or blocked addresses) are checked first, carry no weight, and failing one drops an option whatever its total; all three options pass.
L1's reason: Notifications keeps MailKitEmailSender, which today connects to Mailpit without TLS, so only TLS and login settings are added, no new sender class.
The product owner and team lead fixed the weights before the first test send, while nobody had seen any option's score, so they cannot be pulled toward a preferred option.
Weights: K1 inbox delivery 30, K2 per-email bounce reporting 20, K3 3-year TCO incl. team time 25, K4 exit terms 15, K5 incident support 10; total 100; each row has a reason and a source.

Scores are on a 1-5 scale (5 best), each row citing its evidence; e.g. B's K1 5 rests on a 1,000-email test send with 97% in the main inbox, A's K4 5 on a sample contract keeping data 30 days then deleting with confirmation; all figures assumed.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/email-service-evaluation.md @ stage-4 lines 57-78 (rows K1 Dịch vụ B, K4 Dịch vụ A); lines 3-5 for 'giả định'

claims.text: Weighted totals (max 500): A 390, B 385, self-run 210; A's K1 row is 4 × 30 = 120. B scored higher than A on the test send (K1 5 vs 4).

Sensitivity check: each weight moved 10 up or down, the difference shared equally (2.5 each) over the other four so the total stays 100; A and B swap in five of ten cases, gap at most 25 of 500; self-run last in every case because operating time pulls K3 and K5 down.

ADR 0024 chooses Dịch vụ A on two contract terms not among the scored criteria: API-version change/retirement notice 6 months (A) vs 1 month (B); blocked-address list export any time via API (A) vs monthly via admin page (B); both assumed. L3 asks only whether export is possible, not how often.

ADR 0024 points to email-service-evaluation.md instead of copying the matrix, and its 'Ý kiến đã nhận' answers a backend developer who asked why not B: the gap was not enough, since changing one weight changes the order.

Adding scores lets a very bad score on one criterion be made up for by good scores elsewhere; reduced ATAM keeps each scenario separate for that reason; anything that must not be traded away belongs in a knock-out criterion.
claims.source_hint: design.l4.reduced-atam five-line summary line 4; outline items 1-2

claims.text: When the sensitivity check leaves the order unchanged, the total is a firm result; when it flips, the options are close and a reason outside the matrix decides, recorded in the ADR rather than added as a new weight after scoring.
Weights changed after scores are known can be bent toward a preferred option; every weight and score is a judgement, which the matrix makes visible and disputable one at a time rather than objective.

claims.text: Try it: with K1 40, K2 20, K3 25, K4 5, K5 10 and scores A 4,4,3,5,4 / B 5,3,4,3,3, totals are A 380 and B 405.
SMTP is the standard protocol a program uses to hand an email to a sending server; a bounced email is one returned as undeliverable; Mailpit only catches email and does not deliver it.
